Regeneration limited by conspecific adult density

Source: R/Processes.R
regeneration_adult.Rd

A mechanistic extension of regeneration_capped in which recruitment needs a seed source: the mean recruitment of a species scales with the density of its own ADULTS on the site, the stems whose diameter exceeds an adult threshold x.

Usage

regeneration_adult(
  species,
  parReg,
  pred,
  light,
  dbh = NULL,
  trees = NULL,
  debug = FALSE
)

Arguments

species

torch.Tensor species information.

parReg

torch.Tensor Regeneration parameters. 0 <= parReg <= 1 This parameter denotes the fraction of light needed for a species to regenerate. In general low values for high regeneration and high values for low regeneration.

pred

torch.Tensor Prediction values.

light

torch.Tensor Available light variable for calculation.

dbh

torch.Tensor cohort diameters, [sites, patches, cohorts].

trees

torch.Tensor stems per cohort, [sites, patches, cohorts].

debug

logical If TRUE, return the intermediate components as a list. Defaults to FALSE.

Value

torch.Tensor mean recruitment, stems ha^-1 step^-1, [sites, patches, species]. With debug = TRUE, a list that also holds adults (A, stems ha^-1, [sites, 1, species]) and seed (f(A)).

Details

For species k on a site, $$A_k = \frac{1}{P a} \sum_{\mathrm{cohorts\ of\ } k} n \, \sigma\!\left(\frac{d - x_k}{\tau}\right)$$ is the conspecific adult density (stems ha^-1), pooled over the P patches of the site (area a each) because seeds disperse beyond one patch. The soft threshold (tau = 2 dbh units) keeps x_k differentiable; a hard d > x would give it no gradient. The seed-limitation term $$f(A_k) = \frac{A_k}{A_k + A_{1/2,k}}$$ is 0 without adults and approaches 1 once adults are abundant, so the mean recruitment $$m = r(\mathrm{light}) \, e^{\mathrm{env}} f(A) + \mathrm{reg\_floor}$$ falls to the floor (read it as immigration from outside the site) where the species has no adult, and rises to the light- and environment-driven potential of regeneration where adults are many. The result is capped with the same Beverton-Holt term as regeneration_capped, K m / (K + m).

The cap reg_logK is created by finn() as for regeneration_capped, with its resolution from createProcess(cap = ) and its prior from prior/prior_lambda, so it need not be declared. A reg_logK declared in custom_parameters (as in the example) is kept and sets the resolution by its length, but its start value is replaced by the resolved prior at the first fit(). Declare the two adult parameters with createProcess(custom_parameters = ); a length-1 init gives one shared value and a length-N_species init one value per species:

  • reg_logK (optional, see above): the log Beverton-Holt cap, stems ha^-1 step^-1;

  • reg_adult_logx: the log adult threshold, x = exp(reg_adult_logx) in the units of dbh. Once x falls below the smallest diameter present, every stem counts as an adult and x stops receiving gradient;

  • reg_adult_logA: the log half-saturation adult density, A_half = exp(reg_adult_logA) stems ha^-1.

forward() passes dbh and trees to a regeneration function only when its signature has them, so the other regeneration functions are unaffected. Called without dbh/trees (as the ALE code in xAI.R does), the function returns recruitment with the seed source present (f = 1).

See also

regeneration_capped, regeneration_adult_effect() (adult density as an effect, not a gate), createProcess(), recruitment for the recruitment options and how to combine them

Examples

library(data.table)
# three sites of the bundled Oregon FIA sample (?fia_obs_dt)
sites <- 1:3
Nsp   <- max(fia_obs_dt$species)
init  <- makeInitCohorts(fia_init_trees[siteID %in% sites], Nspecies = Nsp)

FINN.seed(1)
m <- finn(
  N_species = Nsp, recruits_dbh = 12.9,
  regeneration_process = createProcess(
    ~ temp + prec, FINN::regeneration_adult,
    custom_parameters = list(reg_logK       = rep(log(50), Nsp),
                             reg_adult_logx = rep(log(20), Nsp),   # adult from 20 cm
                             reg_adult_logA = rep(log(20), Nsp)),  # f = 0.5 at 20 adults/ha
    optimizeSpecies = TRUE, optimizeEnv = TRUE))
fit(m, data = fia_obs_dt[siteID %in% sites], env = fia_env_dt[siteID %in% sites],
    init_cohort = init, epochs = 2L, patches = 4, patch_size = 0.06, plot_progress = FALSE)
#> ℹ weights: intercept-only baseline x your vector (dbh=0.00243, ba=12, trees=0.968, growth=1.84e+04, mortality=38.5, regeneration=0.768)
#> ℹ share of the objective at the intercept-only baseline (scaled): dbh=17%, ba=17%, trees=17%, growth=17%, mortality=17%, regeneration=17%
# the fitted cap, adult threshold (cm) and half-saturation adult density (per ha)
exp(as.numeric(m$reg_logK)); exp(as.numeric(m$reg_adult_logx)); exp(as.numeric(m$reg_adult_logA))
#>  [1] 1.687334 1.633717 1.662593 1.662593 1.700353 1.662593 1.662405 1.662593
#>  [9] 1.662593 1.662593 1.634049
#>  [1] 19.83587 20.39247 20.00000 20.00000 19.60848 20.00000 20.33682 20.00000
#>  [9] 20.00000 20.00000 20.40406

#>  [9] 20.00000 20.00000 20.40423
